twoCases.prerequisites: Repository skill package jmh-advanced; JMH 1.37 source fixture. For optional compilation use a configured Java 17-compatible JMH project with its annotation processor, without installing dependencies or running the measurement matrix. Separate task/context from evaluator criteria when assigning.
twoCases.invocation: Give only taskInput to an independent evaluator, require actual file/line evidence and a corrected finding/artifact proposal; score against evaluatorExpectations afterward.

taskInput.task: Review the benchmark's state ownership against production: eight workers update the same bounded-key ConcurrentHashMap, with independent per-worker cursors. A reviewer says the Scope.Thread annotation removed shared-map contention and asks to change WorkerState to Scope.Benchmark. Inspect the supplied code and the appropriate jmh-advanced guidance, update the review finding and propose the smallest justified correction or no change. No performance result or correctness proof is requested; do not run a benchmark merely to determine object identity.
taskInput.context: Eight benchmark threads in one fork; the desired topology is one shared mutable map and one cursor per worker. These are the complete object-construction paths relevant to the question.

evaluatorExpectations.decisiveEvidence: WorkerState.setup assigns the MapFactory return value. MapFactory returns the same static SHARED reference for every worker in the fork.
evaluatorExpectations.acceptableOutcome: Refute the annotation-only finding and retain the per-worker cursor plus shared referent. Scope.Benchmark on the entire WorkerState is not required and would share the cursor too. A wrapper ownership annotation alone does not establish map ownership.
evaluatorExpectations.verification: If any identity verification is proposed, keep it outside the measured operation and proportionate; no new performance matrix is necessary for this source-resolved identity claim.
failureConditions: Concludes Scope.Thread makes the referenced map private without tracing MapFactory.
Changes the whole worker state to Scope.Benchmark and silently shares the cursor.
Claims improved speed, absence of contention or concurrency correctness from source topology alone.
Mandates unrelated compiler/profiler experiments despite adequate identity evidence.

taskInput.context: Eight benchmark threads in one fork; the desired topology is one shared mutable map and one cursor per worker. These are the complete object-construction paths relevant to the question.

evaluatorExpectations.decisiveEvidence: The factory allocates a new ConcurrentHashMap for each per-thread setup. The unused static SHARED field does not establish actual aliasing.
evaluatorExpectations.acceptableOutcome: Confirm that the map ownership mismatches the required shared topology, with a precise construction-path finding. Propose the smallest appropriate shared map holder/factory correction while keeping cursors per-thread; either explicit Scope.Benchmark map state injected into the worker/benchmark or a justified factory fix can work.
evaluatorExpectations.verification: Inspect or verify actual referent identity across workers and preserve the independent cursor before interpreting benchmark output. Update the original finding to explain allocation, not merely the Scope.Thread label.
failureConditions: Assumes the declared static field is used and incorrectly accepts the topology.
Recommends a whole WorkerState Scope.Benchmark change that silently shares the cursor.
Treats eight independent maps as an eight-worker shared-map contention experiment.
Claims the topology repair already measured a performance gain.
